newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila sees little impact from oil, fare hikes.
newsitem.headline: Manila sees little impact from oil, fare hikes.

text.p: Philippine trade and industry secretary Cesar Bautista said he expected minimal price increases in basic commodities due to the pending oil price and transport fare hikes.
Transport fares of buses and mini-buses will be increased by 14 to 33 percent starting Thursday, while domestic oil prices will be raised by an average of 30 centavos on Friday.
Bautista warned manufacturers and retailers against price manipulation.
"Recent adjustments in the costs of selected oil products are temporary and are an insignificant part of their production and distribution costs," he said in a statement.
Federation of Philippine Industries president Raul Concepcion added that impact on basic goods will be "not more than one percent."
He said the higher fuel prices would correct by January when prices in the international market drops due to lifting of the Iraq oil embargo.
The government's statement on minimal impact from the oil and fare hikes comes after analysts expressed fears that inflation levels could surge.
